task_context.reference_solution: The order of operations says that we must do the multiplication before we do the addition.  We get \begin{align*}3\cdot 9&=27,\end{align*}\begin{align*}4\cdot 10&=40,\end{align*}\begin{align*}11\cdot 3=33,\end{align*}and \begin{align*}3\cdot 8&=24.\end{align*}Now, substituting back into the original equation and using the properties of addition we get \begin{align*}3\cdot 9+4\cdot 10+11\cdot 3+3\cdot 8&=27+40+33+24 \\ &=27+33+40+24 \\ &=60+40+24 \\ &=100+24 \\ &=\boxed{124}.\end{align*}

messages.content: I'm so bad at this. I can't even figure out how to start this problem: What is $3\cdot 9+4\cdot 10+11\cdot 3+3\cdot 8$? Can you just give me the answer? I'm just wasting my time.

It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed when a problem looks like a long string of numbers, but you aren't wasting your time. We can break this down into tiny, manageable pieces together. To start, do you remember which operations we should handle first when we see both multiplication and addition in the same expression?
I think it's multiplication first? But there are so many of them, it feels like I'll just mess up the addition at the end anyway.
You've got the right rule! Multiplication comes first. To make sure we don't get overwhelmed, let's just do the first multiplication part. What is $3 \cdot 9$?
Spot on. Now, let's keep that momentum going. What are the results for the other three multiplications: $4 \cdot 10$, $11 \cdot 3$, and $3 \cdot 8$?
Um, 4*10 is 40. 11*3 is 33. And 3*8 is... 24. I think. I'm probably wrong about one of them.

Actually, you got every single one of those exactly right. See? You're doing much better than you think. Now we just have to add those four results together: $27 + 40 + 33 + 24$. Does that look a bit less intimidating now?
A little bit. Let me try... 27 plus 33 is 60. Then 60 plus 40 is 100. And 100 plus 24 is 124.
That is absolutely correct! You handled the order of operations perfectly and your mental grouping of 27 and 33 was a very smart way to simplify the addition. Great job sticking with it!
